title: Convert Binary Number in a Linked List to Integer
prompt:
You are given `head`, the head of a singly linked list where each node's value is either `0` or `1`. The list represents a binary number, with the most significant bit first. Return the decimal value of that number.

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,0,1]` represents `1 -> 0 -> 1 -> null`, i.e. binary `101`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, then walk it to compute the decimal value.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 30]
hints: You could build a binary string and convert it, but you can compute the value directly in a single pass.
Process the list from the most significant bit (the head) toward the least significant bit (the tail).
Each time you see a new bit, the running total so far represents a number that is one bit short — shift it left by multiplying by 2, then add the new bit.

solution.approach: Walk the list from head to tail, maintaining a running decimal value. At each node, the existing running value represents all bits seen so far; shifting it left by one bit position (multiplying by 2) makes room for the new least-significant bit, which is added in. By the time the list ends, this running value equals the full binary number's decimal equivalent.
